To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) the performance of systems in the 3-way task was lower than in the 2-way task, and (ii) there was no clear winner of the 3-way challenge.

(i) the 2-way task is much harder than the 3-way task, which in turn is harder than the 2-way challenge of RTE-3; (ii) the best system is still not able to solve the 3-way challenge; (iii) the best systems are able to solve the majority of the 2-way and 3-way tasks; (iv) the best systems perform better in the 2-way than in the 3-way tasks.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3-way task is a challenging task, which is not trivial to tackle, even with the use of sophisticated machine learning algorithms.
the 3-way task is more difficult than the 2-way task, and the results achieved by systems that participated in both are compared to highlight differences between the two tasks.
